column1: # config/r3-11-reel.tsv -- what R3-11's artefact shows, as DATA.
# `tools/replay-capture.py reel config/r3-11-reel.tsv` replays these captures
# into a terminal at true wire speed, in order, with a title before each.  Point
# a screen recorder at the terminal and the artefact is finished -- and, unlike
# a recording, it is REPRODUCIBLE: every byte comes from a committed capture and
# anyone who clones this repository can re-run the same command.
# 🔴 EVERY SEGMENT IS A COMMITTED CAPTURE, and the reel may not contain
# anything else.  A reel that mixed a re-enactment in with real captures would
# be a recording again, and the whole reason this file exists is that it cannot.
# `tools/replay-capture.py reel <this file> --budget` prints the arithmetic
# below without playing anything, and `--self-test` `R15`/`R16`/`R17` assert it.
# The numbers in this comment are therefore a RESTATEMENT of something the tool
# re-derives, not the only place they live.
# prefix<TAB>title<TAB>pause-seconds
# 量 2026-08-31 (TWENTIETH session), every segment through
# `replay-capture verify`:
#   TOTAL                                                            = 59.749 s
# `plan/ARTIFACTS.md` §2 asks for a v0.2 take of **60 s**.  This is 0.25 s
# under it, and `R16` is the case that will go red if a future edit crosses it.
# 🔴 THE PAUSE COLUMN IS SET FROM LEGIBILITY AND THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE
# CEILING, NOT FITTED TO IT.  The pause is the gap AFTER a segment -- 讀,
# `reel()` prints the title, plays, then sleeps -- so it is reading time for
# what just appeared.  2.0 s everywhere; 2.5 s on the two segments whose whole
# content arrives in under a tenth of a second and has to be read rather than
# watched (`W-5b`, 111 bytes in 0.062 s, and `M-d`, 78 bytes in 0.048 s).
# `W-5b` went 2.0 -> 2.5 today for that reason and no other: it is the single
# frame carrying the discriminator, and a viewer who cannot read it has watched
# a router with a light on.
# 🔄 2026-08-31 (twentieth): THE SHORTFALL IS CLOSED, AND IT WAS CLOSED WITH
# CAPTURE RATHER THAN WITH PAUSE.  This file used to say:
#    0.048 + 3.099 = 11.56 s of capture plus 12.5 s of pauses = ~24 s.
#    PROGRESS.md calls this *the 60-second artefact* and at these pauses it is
#    not sixty seconds.  The number to change is the pause column, not the
#    captures -- padding a reel with dead terminal is worse than a short one."
# and then, later the same day:
#   "THE PAUSES ARE NOT BEING PADDED ... The other repair is MORE CAPTURE, and
#    seating 8 is about to produce it: probe3's own boot, its UART report and
#    the 718-word read-back.  Setting this column now would be setting it
#    against a reel that is about to grow, so it is set at R3-11 with that
#    material in hand."
# The material arrived and ONE capture of it is in the reel.  Which one, and
# why the other three are not, is the part worth writing down:
#   `bench/2026-08-31c/K-J`  IN.  33.188 s.  It is `probe3`'s execution and its
#       whole UART report (offsets 0..6049, `J 80500000` to `rlxprobe: end`,
#       t=0..~2.4 s) AND THEN, in the same capture, the watchdog firing, the
#       loader re-staging `0x80500000` **from flash**, and the board's own
#       vendor firmware booting end to end (t=2.5..33.188).  ⚠️ It is in the
#       reel as a CONTROL, not as a result: `PROGRESS.md`'s anti-DoD says a
#       banner is not evidence that my kernel ran, because this loader
#       re-stages on a watchdog reset -- and this segment is that trap
#       happening, on video, with `start address: 0x80003440` where segment 1
#       shows `0x80003600`.  A viewer's first objection to segments 1-6 is
#       answered inside the artefact instead of in prose beside it.
#       🔴 68 % of its 33 s is inter-line gap, and that is NOT the dead
#       terminal this file forbids: the gaps are the vendor firmware's own
#       (5.019 s decompressing, 4.400 s in the WLAN driver, 3.416 s after
#       BusyBox's init line).  量, and the comparison that settles it is
#       `W-3`, which is 96 % gap and which nobody calls padded.
#       🟢 Checked before it went in: `grep -aoE '([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}[:-]){5}
#       [0-9A-Fa-f]{2}'` over `K-J.log` returns NOTHING, so the vendor's boot
#       is not printing this unit's MAC into a video.
#   `bench/2026-08-31c/K2b-rb`  OUT.  2.316 s.  The 718-word result block read
#       back out of DRAM.  It is 8,486 bytes of hexadecimal scrolling past in
#       2.3 s and its claim -- *the block was sealed, read back, and `rbcheck`
#       judged it* -- is not visible in the pixels.  That claim belongs in the
#       write-up, where it can be checked.  Adding it would also have put the
#       reel at 64.1 s, over §2's 60.
#   `bench/2026-08-31c/K-A`  OUT, and it is not a judgement call.  25.065 s of
#       which essentially all is `console-capture --esc 25` spamming ESC at the
#       loader: `<RealTek>` `Unknown command !` repeated ~130 times.  Not
#       material.  Same for the last ~50 s of `K2-J` (`--esc-after 60`).
#   `bench/2026-08-31c/K3-rb` / `K4-rb`  OUT.  They are `MEM-17`'s retention
#       readings and they look identical to `K2b-rb` on screen; what separates
#       them is a bit-for-bit comparison, which is a table, not a shot.
# ⚠️ So `probe3`'s run and its UART report ARE in the reel and the 718-word
# read-back is NOT, where the sentence above proposed all three.  The two that
# went in went in inside one capture, because they cannot be separated -- a
# reel row is one whole capture, by construction.
# The order is R3's own DoD, D1 through D5, and then the control -- claim
# first, then the thing that says the claim is not the vendor's.  🔴 That
# order is deliberate in one more way: a viewer who stops at 20 s has seen
# D1-D5 complete.  Opening with the vendor's 33 s would have shown a viewer who
# stops early nothing but Realtek's boot.

column2: D1-D4  my kernel boots from RAM to a shell
D2  and the build stamp is mine, not the vendor's
D4  a typed command returns output
the whole 4 MiB read back through my MTD path
and the flash cannot be written through it
CONTROL  probe3 reports, the watchdog fires, and the VENDOR's own firmware boots
